CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit to evaluate the response to medication adjustments for generalized anxiety disorder, insomnia, persistent fatigue, and tension-type headaches, and to assess the overall impact on quality of life.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns for his follow-up appointment, expressing a mixture of relief and ongoing challenges regarding his mental health management. He reports that the adjustment to trazodone has yielded some improvement in his insomnia, stating that he is now able to initiate sleep more easily and experiences fewer nocturnal awakenings. He is currently taking trazodone at 100 mg nightly, which he finds more effective than the previous dosage. However, he still experiences occasional episodes of heightened anxiety, particularly during work-related pressures.
Despite these improvements, Mr. Smith notes that his anxiety remains a concern, particularly in high-stress situations. He has been utilizing lorazepam 1 mg as needed, which he finds helpful for acute episodes of anxiety. He acknowledges that while CBT continues to provide him with valuable coping strategies, he may benefit from additional therapeutic support, possibly through group therapy.
Mr. Smith reports that his tension-type headaches have persisted, occurring approximately once a week with an intensity rating of 5 to 7 out of 10. He has been adhering to the increased ibuprofen dosage of 600 mg as needed, which has provided moderate relief; however, he notes that the frequency of headaches correlates with his stress levels, particularly during project deadlines at work. He continues to maintain his headache diary, which he feels is instrumental in identifying triggers.
His persistent fatigue remains a significant issue, although he reports that the addition of bupropion at 150 mg daily has contributed positively to his energy levels and mood stabilization. He states that he feels more alert during the day and is better able to engage in his physical activities, including yoga and brisk walking, which he finds beneficial for both his physical and mental health.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 300 mg daily (continued) 2. Trazodone 100 mg at bedtime (increased dosage for improved efficacy) 3. Lisinopril 10 mg daily (continued) 4. Ibuprofen 600 mg as needed for headache relief (continued) 5. Amitriptyline 50 mg nightly (continued) 6. Topiramate 150 mg daily (continued) 7. Lorazepam 1 mg as needed (continued) 8. Melatonin 3 mg at bedtime (continued) 9. Modafinil 100 mg in the morning (continued) 10. Bupropion 150 mg daily (newly initiated)
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith reports continued engagement in physical activities, including yoga and brisk walking, which he finds beneficial for his mental health. He has maintained a balanced diet and has further reduced his caffeine intake. He acknowledges that while he is managing his stress better through mindfulness and meditation, work-related pressures still pose challenges to his overall well-being.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Improved management of anxiety; sleep disturbances have decreased; no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms reported. - Neurological: Stable headache frequency; no dizziness or visual disturbances noted. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or dyspnea. - General: Persistent fatigue, though improved; no fever or significant weight changes.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 122/76 mmHg, HR 68 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.6F - General: Alert, oriented; appears well-rested; mood appears stable with mild anxiety. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no motor or sensory deficits observed; no tenderness in the temporal region. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative; maintains good eye contact; mood appears stable with mild anxiety.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline at 300 mg daily. Maintain lorazepam for acute anxiety management, with a plan to reassess in one month. 2. Insomnia: Continue trazodone at 100 mg at bedtime, monitoring for efficacy and side effects. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Continue topiramate at 150 mg daily; recommend continuing ibuprofen at 600 mg as needed. If symptoms persist, consider referral to a neurologist. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Continue bupropion at 150 mg daily; encourage ongoing physical activity and stress management techniques.
Follow-up appointment is scheduled for 2029-11-14 to evaluate symptom progression, medication adjustments, and address any new concerns. Mr. Smith is encouraged to maintain detailed records of his symptoms and medication responses to facilitate ongoing management.
